summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, status post TIPS placement, bladder and prostate cancer with ileal conduit and nephrostomy tube, was readmitted one day after discharge for recurrent hematochezia, melena, and hematemesis. He reported ongoing dizziness and significant blood loss per rectum. Evaluation included a liver ultrasound, which confirmed a patent TIPS and cirrhotic liver without ascites or portal vein thrombosis. His hemoglobin remained stable during this admission, and he did not require transfusion. He was managed conservatively with acid-suppression therapy and close monitoring. The patient showed clinical improvement with no further bleeding episodes and was discharged with instructions to follow up with his specialists, avoid alcohol, and monitor for recurrent symptoms. He was advised to continue home medications and avoid NSAIDs due to bleeding risk.
